fix.shows: From the bid papers on GeM, the Internet Freedom Foundation reports that the Office of the Registrar General bought 96 Esri ArcGIS licences for Census 2027 under a Proprietary Article Certificate, which rules out competition on the product, on a file numbered XII-027/23/2019-MAP and carried forward from 2019. It reports that the contract went on 10 June 2026 to Corporate Infotech Private Limited for ₹14,38,74,322, after four resellers of the same Esri India product bid within 0.95 per cent of each other in a reverse auction, and that its scope covers the Houselisting Block Creator, the Census Thematic Mapper and the Digital District Census Hand Book in every state and union territory. Citing a ReliaQuest report of October 2025, IFF says a group that ReliaQuest assessed with moderate confidence to be the Chinese state-sponsored Flax Typhoon kept a backdoor in an unnamed organisation's ArcGIS Server for over a year, and that Esri put the compromise down to the victim's configuration and issued no patch. IFF notes that the work in the bid covers boundaries, maps and tabulated data and does not route individual records or caste answers through Esri's software directly. It finds no public record of a security audit, of CERT-In clearance or of the reasons for passing over Bhuvan and open-source tools, and it has filed RTI applications. The piece concerns the Census mapping software and says nothing about the electoral rolls, the SIR or the National Population Register.

note: Second reading, 1 November 2026: the Internet Freedom Foundation's piece by Vikram Raj read afresh in full from the page with curl (the page gives 31 October 2026 and its article:published_time is 2026-10-31T12:36:56+05:30). Opened from IFF's Google Drive folder: the GeM bid document GEM/2026/B/7370593 of 29 April 2026 (Ministry of Home Affairs, Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, total quantity 96, PAC only, CA approval number XII-027/23/2019-Map, bid end 9 May 2026, reverse auction with H1-highest priced bid elimination, MII purchase preference yes), the Proprietary Article Certificate (file XII-027/23/2019-MAP dated 7 April 2026, Rs 8,75,02,463 a year, finance wing Note 411 of 24 April 2026, prior GeM contract of 12 February 2024 with CIPL, signed by Vaduguru V L N Sarma on 29 April 2026), the Additional Terms and Conditions (32 Desktop Advanced, 49 Desktop Standard and 11 Enterprise Advanced upgrades and 4 new Indo ArcGIS Developer Builder licences, 96 in all, with support for the HLB Creator, Boundary Management, the Digital Administrative Atlas, the Census Thematic Mapper and the District Census Hand Book maps, and 'Other Offices' defined as the DCOs at all state and union territory capitals) and GeM's general terms. The award of 10 June 2026 (Corporate Infotech at Rs 14,38,74,322, four bidders, L4 0.95 per cent above L1) is not in that folder and GeM did not answer from the sandbox, so those figures rest on IFF's account of the award page, and the summary gives them as IFF's report. ReliaQuest's report (14 October 2025) was read: it attributes the attack 'with high confidence to Chinese APTs and with moderate confidence to Flax Typhoon' and gives year-long access, so the moderate-confidence qualifier is carried. Esri's trust blog refused the fetch (403), so the account of Esri's response is IFF's and is attributed to IFF in the summary. The four quotes are verbatim. A search of the full text and the raw page for electoral, elector, voter, roll, SIR, intensive revision, NPR, Population Register and Election Commission finds none; Aadhaar appears once, in IFF's separate representation on the Census schedule. Corrected one point: the first reading said the licences 'will run' the three applications 'in every state'. The piece says the scope ties Esri India into them 'across every State and Union Territory', and the ATC buys maintenance and technical support for them, so the summary now says the contract's scope covers them in every state and union territory. Title, outlet, author, date and free access checked. Group 'Investigations' and type 'article (investigation)' fit, as for The Reporters' Collective's procurement and software reports. The summary names no private person and passes the writing rules.
